title: Indra and Virochana learn from Prajapati — the body is not the self (8.7–8.8)
hook: a god and a demon study for thirty-two years, are told to look in a pan of water, and both walk away thinking the reflection is the self

segments.voice: Yesterday: dahara, a small space as large as all space. Your line was the space in the heart. Today ends week four of year two.

A mirror by the front door. Good shirt. Hair right. That's me, says the glance, before any thought. Then a selfie: me again. Then a tagged photo from ten years ago: somehow, also me. People point at a lot of pictures and say me. The Chandogya tells of two students who did exactly that, and one of them took the mistake home and built a whole philosophy on it.
screen: `GOOD SHIRT. HAIR RIGHT.` → `THAT'S ME.` → `WE POINT AT PICTURES AND SAY ME.`

segments.voice: Prajapati, the lord of creatures, announces: there is a self free from evil, from old age and death, from grief, hunger and thirst. Whoever finds it gains all worlds. The gods and the demons both hear. The gods send their king, Indra. The demons send theirs, Virochana. The two rivals arrive with firewood in their hands, not speaking to each other, and live as students for thirty-two years. Then Prajapati teaches: the person seen in the eye, that is the self. Immortal, fearless. That is Brahman. They ask: and the one seen in water, or in a mirror? It's seen in all these, he says. Look at yourselves in a pan of water. What do you see? Our whole selves, sir, down to the hair and the nails. Now dress up well, put on ornaments, and look again. Just as we are, sir, well dressed and adorned, so are these two. That is the self, says Prajapati, immortal, fearless. Both leave content. Prajapati watches them go: they go without having found the self. Shankara and other commentators say he meant the seer behind the eye, and the students heard the image in the eye. Virochana goes home and teaches the demons that the body is the self: honor it, adorn it, serve it. Indra sets off too, but on the road, something starts to bother him. This week, from the top: truth protects. Narada, a knower of words. The ladder, from name up to rain. The infinite. The space in the heart. And today, two students mistaking the reflection for the one who sees.
screen: `A SELF FREE FROM DEATH AND GRIEF.` · `THIRTY-TWO YEARS AS STUDENTS.` · `LOOK IN A PAN OF WATER.` · `THE WEEK, FROM THE TOP.` · then, large: `THE REFLECTION ISN'T YOU.`

segments.voice: Picture your face in a mirror, clearly, and then ask gently: who's looking? Don't answer with words; turn your attention back toward the looking itself, like turning around in a doorway, and each time you drift back to the picture, turn around again.
Prajapati, lord of creatures. A god and a demon look in a pan of water, adorned, and both mistake the reflection for the self Prajapati described.
Your line: the reflection isn't you. On the road, Indra isn't so sure. Week four of year two, done.

screen: `DAY 357 COUNTS.` → `WEEK FOUR OF YEAR TWO, DONE.` → `TOMORROW: INDRA RETURNS.`

howItsDone: Vedanta teachers often use the story of Indra and Virochana to introduce the difference between the body and the self, and the story's stages are read as a step-by-step inquiry into who we are.

pairs: where they look for the self

myth: Indra and Virochana came together as friends

fork.setup: you're Indra. you've seen yourself, well dressed and adorned, in a pan of water, and Prajapati has said: that is the self. what do you do?
options: set off, but begin to have doubts on the road.
fork.reveal: Virochana goes home satisfied. Indra sets off too, but something starts to bother him, and tomorrow he comes back.

original.note: Sanskrit prajāpati: lord of creatures, the creator figure who teaches Indra and Virochana.

trapdoor: what you thought: a myth about gods and demons.
what it means: the first and easiest mistake about the self is to point at the body, the reflection, and say that's me.
what a scholar hears: Chandogya 8.7–8.8; commentators read Prajapati's 'person seen in the eye' as the seer, which the students hear as the image in the pupil.
recall: the dear one, the one who is adored
guess: lord of creatures, who teaches Indra and Virochana
the king of the demons, Indra's rival student
the king of the gods who goes back to learn more

chat.says: What did Virochana get wrong in that mirror story?
options: He took the reflection, the body, for the self, and taught the demons that.
He refused to study and left before Prajapati taught him anything.
He thought the self was the dreamer, not the one awake and seeing.
chat.meaning: Both students saw themselves in a pan of water and left content. Virochana went home teaching that the body is the self.

Prajapati.meaning: lord of creatures, the teacher in this story

Virochana.meaning: king of the demons, Indra's rival

Shankara.meaning: the great teacher of Advaita Vedanta

Narada.meaning: a famous sage, learned in every subject of his day
